brv_wh_delivery_tjure.m: What?! My lucky clover...but why now? Anyway, I'll no longer run out of luck. Here's my delivery fee.

r: What are you doing in such a lonely place?
I'm surprised to see you here as well. Did you order 'Mysterious green something'?

tjure_0_10.m: I am Tjure of Brimhaven. I am ... was ... a successful merchant. But my luck has run out.

tjure_0_12.m: All I can do now is hide in this lonely place, far away from any water.
r: Aha. I won't bother you then.

tjure_0_20.m: I once found a mermaid asleep on the beach of a river, north of here. What a beautiful sight! I could not avert my eyes!

tjure_0_22.m: Especially, the colorful tail attracted me so much, that I did something that I have deeply regretted since then.

tjure_10.m: I pulled out one of her shimmering, dazzling scales, and ran away.

r: No problem. By the way, did you order a 'Mysterious green something'?

tjure_10_10.m: The mermaid immediately awoke and was very angry. But on land she had no chance to catch me.

tjure_20.m: Crying and sobbing, the mermaid called after me. Finally, she screamed at me that I would never find peace, and that I would never want to approach water again!

tjure_200.m: Oh, you look better than the last time we met. Thank you for your help.
r: Indeed. By the way, did you order a 'Mysterious green something'?

tjure_30.m: At first I was happy with my shimmering scale. But I soon realized that everything in my life was going wrong.

tjure_30_10.m: I couldn't think of anything else but the wrath of the people of the river.

tjure_30_20.m: What could I do? I tried to throw it away or give it to other people - all in vain.

tjure_30_30.m: I traveled all over Dhayavar to find someone to help me. Finally, a wise woman, far in the northeast, listened to my story. She advised me to return the scale to the mermaid. This would break the curse.

tjure_30_32.m: But I did not dare to do this.

tjure_30_34.m: She told me that my only other option was to find some kind-hearted person to buy it from me, but then they take on the curse.
r: Let me be the one to rescue you. Sell me the scale.

tjure_30_40.m: I know, I know. When they heard my story, everybody ran away.
r: That's too bad. I hope that you will find someone to buy it. Bye.
Not me. I will buy the scale.

tjure_30_50.m: So you really won't help me? You will leave me to my misery?
r: Sorry, I can't do it. Bye.
I have to think about it.
OK. maybe I am stupid, but sell me the scale.

tjure_30_90.m: Here, take it! I have to request gold for it, otherwise it won't work. But one piece of gold should be enough.
r: No problem, here, take the gold.

tjure_30_92.m: (As soon as you take the scale in your hands, a great sluggishness and a feeling of despair come over you.)

tjure_30_94.m: (For a second you feel very dizzy. At least you manage not to faint. As from afar you hear a voice.)

tjure_90.m: *Sigh* You were my last hope. Leave me now.
r: OK. One question before I go: did you order a 'Mysterious green something'?

tjure_wh_delivery_90.m: *Sigh* You were my last hope. Leave me now.
r: Not until I have delivered this to you. Are you the one who ordered a 'Mysterious green something'?

brv_wh_delivery.10: Facutloni asked me to help him deliver all of the items ordered by his customers a long time ago. He even gave me an old document with the names and items written on it.
brv_wh_delivery.20: Arcir the Fallhaven book-lover ordered a 'Dusty Old book'.
brv_wh_delivery.30: Edrin the Brimhaven metalsmith ordered a 'Striped Hammer'.
brv_wh_delivery.40: Odirath the Stoutford armorer ordered a 'Pretty Porcelain Figure'.
brv_wh_delivery.50: Venanra the Brimhaven laundress ordered an 'Old, worn cape'.
brv_wh_delivery.60: Tjure the unlucky Brimhaven merchant ordered a 'Mysterious green something'.
brv_wh_delivery.70: Servant the Guynmart servant ordered a 'Chandelier'.
brv_wh_delivery.80: Arghes at Remgard tavern ordered 'Yellow boots'.
brv_wh_delivery.90: Wyre the mournful Vilegard woman ordered a 'Lyre'.
brv_wh_delivery.110: Pangitain the Brimhaven fortune teller ordered a 'Crystal Globe'.
brv_wh_delivery.120: Facutloni wants me to report back after the deliveries are complete.
brv_wh_delivery.130: I reported back to Facutloni. He is very happy.

mermaid_scale.10: In a clearing, you met Tjure, who desperately asked for your help. He had once found a mermaid asleep on the beach at the river. The colorful tail attracted him so much that he pulled out a dazzling scale and ran away.
mermaid_scale.20: Crying and mourning, the mermaid called after him. Finally she cursed him. Since then, Tjure has never been happy. He just wanted to get rid of the scale. Nevertheless, he never ventured back to the vicinity of the river.
mermaid_scale.30: A wise woman told Tjure that he could neither throw away nor destroy the scale. His only salvation would be to give it back or to have someone buy it from him. But who would ever want to incur the wrath of a mermaid?
mermaid_scale.90: You decided not to help Tjure.
mermaid_scale.100: As soon as you held the scale in your hands, a great sluggishness and dispair came over you.
mermaid_scale.200: You put the scale on the mark on the ground.
mermaid_scale.210: There rang out a beautiful song of gratitude.
mermaid_scale.220: You found a heavy bag of gold.
